title: Sagaing Kingdom
capsule: The Sagaing Kingdom was a short-lived Burmese successor state in the Mu valley of Upper Myanmar, established when Prince Saw Yun seceded from the Pinya kingdom around 1315–1326 and founded a new capital at Sagaing on the Irrawaddy River's west bank. The kingdom owed its survival to internal Pinya divisions rather than military strength, and cultivated close ties with politically powerful forest-dwelling Buddhist monks who provided legitimacy. Devastating Shan raids from Maw between 1356 and 1364 fatally weakened both Sagaing and Pinya; after Pinya switched allegiance to the invaders, Sagaing fell in April 1364, and Thado Minbya immediately founded the Ava kingdom on 26 February 1365 by uniting the ruins of both principalities, establishing a polity that would dominate Upper Myanmar for the next two centuries.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sagaing Kingdom's territorial extent is poorly attested; it is largely reconstructed from Burmese chronicles whose reliability for this period is debated among specialists.
